authority_limit: Rust traits encode type-level interface obligations; they do not by themselves express domain laws, effects, total failures, resource bounds or conformance evidence.
claim_scope: abstract interfaces, implementations, associated functions/types/constants and bounds
title: The Rust Reference — Traits

authority_limit: WIT describes component interfaces and bindings, not business semantics, algebraic laws, provider quality or end-to-end behavior.
claim_scope: typed imports/exports, resources, worlds and cross-language component interfaces
title: WebAssembly Interface Types (WIT)

authority_limit: The paper proves convergence under explicit assumptions; it does not make arbitrary merges semantically valid or establish application invariants, authorization or loss acceptance.
claim_scope: convergence conditions for state- and operation-based replicated data types
title: Conflict-free Replicated Data Types

authority_limit: Covers mediation between stream components; it does not define transformations, business ordering, durability, exactly-once effects or all runtime resource policies.

title: Reactive Streams JVM Specification 1.0.4

authority_limit: Defines an HTTP representation for interface problems, not an internal exception model, retry policy, root cause, compensation result or universal domain refusal catalog.

title: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs

authority_limit: A model proves only encoded properties within its abstraction and assumptions; it does not prove implementation refinement, environment behavior or product fitness without further evidence.
claim_scope: state-machine specifications using initial states, next-state relation, safety and liveness properties
title: Specifying and Verifying Systems With TLA+

authority_limit: Provenance records origins and relations; it does not establish truth, authorization, causal sufficiency, integrity or acceptance.

title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology

authority_limit: Methodological guidance cannot make an underspecified requirement testable or prove completeness of a test suite or implementation.
